title: kv-prefetch-tuning-and-flashattention-tradeoffs
content:
Summary:

This note captures an experimental sweep focused on how KV prefetch sizing and FlashAttention (FA) kernel selection interact to affect latency tail behavior and throughput for long-sequence workloads. Unlike prior attention-focused notes that concentrated on kernel-level micro-optimizations, this doc tries to tie user-visible metrics (p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/s, and memory pressure) to configuration knobs we can expose in the runtime: kv_prefetch_bytes, prefetch_margin, and attention_fallback_policy. The target is production-style inference for 8k-32k context LLMs on A100/H100 nodes.

Context and motivation:
- We observed sudden p99 spikes when switching from FA-v2 to paged-attention on sequences >16k in the last rollout (see linked Slack thread).
- Hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch reduces kernel stall for FA by ensuring KV pages are resident, but it increases memory pressure and can force prefetched KV eviction during batched concurrent requests, which in turn triggers paged-attention fallbacks that are costlier per-token.
- Goal: find safe prefetch sizing heuristics across batch sizes/seq lengths that minimize p99 without regressing throughput or running out of device memory.

Environment and baseline:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (dgx-1-like) and H100 80GB (test cluster gpu-h100-2).
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v0.38.1-localized, kernel bundle: flashattention-v2.1.0, fused_ops v1.3.0, paged-attn v0.9.
- Framework: PyTorch 2.2.0 + Triton 2.0.1; CUDA 12.1; cuDNN 9.1.
- Model: llama-4x-8k variant trimmed for perf tests (dense weights), serving config: kv_cache_per_request=true, kv_page_size=64MB default.
- Baseline: kv_prefetch_bytes=0 (no prefetch), attention_fallback_policy=allow-paged, batch_size=8, seq_len=8192. Baseline throughput 12.4K tokens/s, p50 token latency 8.2ms, p99 token latency 47.1ms. Memory headroom ~14GB free at start.

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Sweep kv_prefetch_bytes: [0, 8MB, 32MB, 64MB, 128MB]
- Sweep prefetch_margin: [0.0, 0.2, 0.5] (fraction of predicted future KV accesses)
- Batch sizes: [1, 4, 8, 16]
- Seq lengths: [4096, 8192, 16384, 32768]
- Kernel settings: force_flashattention=true/false (to force FA even if paged data); attention_fallback_policy: [allow-paged, disallow-paged-with-fallback-to-smaller-model] (disallow-paged simulated by routing to quantized-8bit variant)

Key commands (repro):
- runner: ./tools/perf_runner.sh --model llama-4x --batch 8 --seq 8192 --kv-prefetch 64MB --prefetch-margin 0.2 --force-fa
- microbench: python benchmarks/attn_micro.py --kernel flashattention --batch 8 --seq 8192 --iters 300 --record-kernel-times
- memory snapshot: nvidia-smi dmon + nvprof kernel timeline (where available)

Representative results (selected slice) - A100, batch=8:

kv_prefetch_bytes | prefetch_margin | throughput (tokens/s) | p50 token (ms) | p99 token (ms) | memory delta (GB)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0                 | 0.0             | 12400                | 8.2            | 47.1           | +0.0
8MB               | 0.2             | 13450                | 7.8            | 39.6           | +1.1
32MB              | 0.2             | 13810                | 7.6            | 31.9           | +4.2
64MB              | 0.2             | 13700                | 7.9            | 35.0           | +8.6
128MB             | 0.5             | 12900                | 8.6            | 62.3           | +16.1

Observations from the slice above:
- Small prefetch (8MB) gives clear tail latency win with modest memory increase. p99 reduced by ~16% and throughput increased ~8% likely due to fewer kernel stalls.
- Medium prefetch (32MB) produced the best p99 in this slice and highest throughput; suggests a knee around 16-48MB for batch=8 / seq=8k on A100.
- Large prefetch (128MB) increases memory pressure enough to trigger eviction cascades when there are concurrent requests, producing worse tails than 32MB and even the no-prefetch baseline in some runs.

Cross-dimensional behavior (high-level):
- Batch size sensitivity: higher batch sizes (16) amplify the memory cost of prefetch; the knee shifts left (smaller prefetch stays optimal). For batch=1, larger prefetch up to 64MB can be tolerated.
- Sequence length: as seq increases to 16k/32k, prefetch payoff increases because larger KV working set benefits more from being resident, but absolute memory cost also scales. On H100 with larger aggregate GPU memory pressure patterns differed: H100 tolerated 64MB prefetch in batch=8 for 16k seq better than A100 due to faster host<->device eviction and higher bandwidth.
- Kernel interactions: forcing FA even when pages are partially absent reduces the fallback to paged-attn but increases mid-latency events due to software-managed copies; letting runtime fallback to paged-attn produces predictable but higher per-token latency.

Microbench kernel timings (example from kernel traces):
- FA forward kernel (per-token) median 0.42ms, 95th 0.51ms.
- Paged-attn page-fetch copy overhead median 0.18ms per page fetch; when triggered mid-request added 12-30ms depending on number of pages touched.
- Fused-ops latency variance increased when prefetch caused greater CUDA allocation churn (observed in tracer).

Root-cause hypotheses and supporting evidence:
1) Eviction cascade: large prefetch increases resident KV and squeezes allocator free space; concurrent allocations for other requests trigger CUDA caching allocator evictions, which cause extra copy-on-demand when KV pages are touched. Evidence: nvprof traces showing increased allocation/free rates and clobbered pinned memory windows correlated with p99 spikes.
2) Suboptimal prefetch granularity: using byte-level prefetch (64MB pages) causes uneven coverage; smaller page sizes with higher-frequency prefetch were more cache-friendly in practice. Evidence: runs where we reduced kv_page_size to 16MB but kept same kv_prefetch_bytes showed lower p99 for identical memory delta.
3) Kernel compatibility: FA expects contiguous KV in-place access patterns; partial page hits lead to software fallbacks that are more expensive than a planned paged-attn strategy. Evidence: requesting force-fa in cases of partial pages increased mid-latency jitter.

Operational recommendations (draft):
- Make kv_prefetch_bytes an adaptive knob: start conservative (8MB) and grow only if observed per-route tail > threshold and memory headroom > X GB.
- Add prefetch_margin heuristic tied to predicted continuation length: e.g., margin = min(0.2, predicted_next_tokens / seq_len).
- Expose a route-level policy: prefetched_allowed = true/false and prefetched_budget (percent of route device memory). When budget exhausted, fall back to paged-attn or lower-quality variant.
- Implement a lightweight allocator guard: track prefetched allocations and refuse prefetch if live_allocator_free < min_free_mb to prevent eviction cascades.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- What's the right default kv_page_size? Our limited tests suggest 16MB page gives better behavior across multi-tenant loads; need more runs with mixed request sizes.
- Can we instrument a low-overhead metric for "prefetch eviction events" to correlate in-prod p99 spikes?
- Should we move to per-model prefetch profiles determined by offline sweep at model onboarding time? (tradeoff: onboarding time vs per-route safety)
- Investigate CUDA allocator tuning (no-op vs c10 caching) to see if eviction cascades can be mitigated without reducing prefetch efficacy.

Short term action items (owner tags):
- Aisha: add adaptive prefetch prototype behind feature flag in runtime (RFC branch) by 2026-03-14.
- Miguel: run mixed-workload sweep (batch 1/8/16 with 4 concurrent clients) on H100 cluster and upload artifacts to the run bucket by 2026-03-07.
- Ravi: proof-of-concept allocator guard that refuses prefetch when free < 8GB; bench and report regressions by 2026-03-09.

Appendix - quick reproducible script snippet:
- export MODEL=llama-4x
- python tools/serve_profile.py --model $MODEL --gpu-type a100 --clients 4 --batch 8 --seq 16384 --kv-prefetch 32MB --prefetch-margin 0.2 --record /tmp/run_prefetch_32mb.json

Notes to self (informal):
- This felt messy to tune; need better sim harness that can emulate many small concurrent requests hitting different parts of KV.
- Try decreasing default kv_page_size to 16MB in a dev cluster to see long-run behavior for Dedicated customers.

References and links (same as linked artifacts) and quick pointers to previous docs: see attention-pipeline-queueing-and-kernel-crosswalk.json and kv-cache-contention-attention-tail-latency-analysis.json for related traces, but this doc intentionally focuses on the interaction of prefetch sizing and kernel selection.

-- Aisha
